reason: Concrete GA4 Data/Admin API report, metadata, account and entity handlers with GTM v2 tools; MCPServer v2 registration via ToolSpec registry.

tools.name: ga4_account_summaries
tools.description:
List every GA4 account and property the authenticated user can access.

This is the entry point for all GA4 work — it returns the property IDs the
other ga4_* tools need.

page_token.description: Pagination token from a previous response.
page_token.title: Page Token

tools.behavior: Lists account summaries with pageSize 200 and optional page token; returns trimmed accounts and property summaries.

tools.name: ga4_admin_create
tools.description:
Create a GA4 custom dimension, custom metric, key event, or data stream on a property.

Defaults to dry-run: nothing is sent until called with dry_run=False.

entity_type.description: What to create: custom_dimensions, custom_metrics, key_events, or data_streams.

body.description: Entity JSON per the Admin API, e.g. a custom dimension: {'parameterName': 'lead_type', 'displayName': 'Lead Type', 'scope': 'EVENT'}.
body.title: Body

dry_run.description: True (default) echoes the request without sending it.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

tools.behavior: Returns the request locally when dry_run is true; otherwise creates the selected property sub-entity using the arbitrary JSON body.
notes: Schema enum also accepts property, but handler rejects creating properties.
Requires write/destructive tier; dry_run defaults true. Arbitrary dict bodies expose additionalProperties=true, not an API-specific body model.

tools.name: ga4_admin_delete
tools.description:
Delete or archive a GA4 entity by resource name. Two-phase.

Custom dimensions/metrics are ARCHIVED (permanent — GA4 has no unarchive
or true delete for them); key events and data streams are DELETED.
Deleting a data stream stops collection for it. Properties cannot be
deleted through this tool by design.

name.description: Full resource name from a read tool, e.g. 'properties/123/customDimensions/456' or 'properties/123/dataStreams/789'.
name.title: Name

confirm_token.description: Omit on the first call — it returns a token and a summary instead of deleting. Pass the token back (same name) to execute.
confirm_token.title: Confirm Token

tools.behavior: First call issues an operation-bound confirmation token. Redeeming it archives a custom dimension/metric or deletes a key event/data stream.
notes: Only four-segment properties/{id}/{collection}/{id} names accepted; collection must be customDimensions, customMetrics, keyEvents or dataStreams. Return key for archive is archived; delete produces deleted.
Requires destructive tier. Confirmation tokens are in-memory, single-use, expire after 600 seconds and bind to exact operation arguments; consumed before API execution.

tools.name: ga4_admin_list
tools.description:
List a GA4 property's sub-entities.

Covers data streams, key events, custom dimensions/metrics, Google Ads
links, and Firebase links.

page_token.description: Pagination token from a previous response.
page_token.title: Page Token

tools.behavior: Dispatches entity type to property resource list and returns items with pagination token.

tools.name: ga4_admin_update
tools.description:
Update a GA4 entity (or the property itself) by resource name. Defaults to dry-run.

Unlike GTM, GA4 updates are partial: only fields named in update_mask change.

entity_type.description: What to update, including 'property' for the property itself.

name.description: Full resource name from a read tool, e.g. 'properties/123/customDimensions/456' or 'properties/123' for the property.
name.title: Name

update_mask.description: Comma-separated field names being updated (e.g. 'displayName,description'), or '*' to update every field present in body.
update_mask.title: Update Mask

dry_run.description: True (default) echoes the request without sending it.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

tools.behavior: Returns the request locally when dry_run is true; otherwise patches the selected resource with the arbitrary JSON body and updateMask.
notes: Resource name must start with properties/; validation does not verify selected entity type matches the name.
Requires write/destructive tier; dry_run defaults true. Arbitrary dict bodies expose additionalProperties=true, not an API-specific body model.

tools.name: ga4_metadata
tools.description:
List the dimension/metric API names available on a property (standard + custom).

Use this before ga4_run_report to find exact API names.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on API/UI names, e.g. 'revenue'.
search.title: Search

tools.behavior: Fetches property metadata, trims dimensions/metrics to API name, UI name and custom flag, optionally filters case-insensitively.

tools.name: ga4_property_get
tools.description: Fetch one GA4 property's full configuration (timezone, currency, industry, service level).
tools.behavior: Normalizes numeric property ID and fetches full property configuration.

tools.name: ga4_run_realtime_report
tools.description: Run a GA4 realtime report (last 30 minutes) — e.g. to verify events are firing now.
tools.behavior: Builds a realtime report; normalizes property ID, executes runRealtimeReport and reshapes response rows.

tools.name: ga4_run_report
tools.description:
Run a GA4 report over a date range and return one dict per row.

Rows are keyed by the requested dimension/metric API names. `row_count` is
the total available on the server; raise `limit` or refine dimensions if
rows were truncated.

metrics.description: Metric API names, e.g. ['sessions', 'conversions', 'totalRevenue']. Discover names via ga4_metadata.
metrics.title: Metrics

tools.behavior: Builds a date-range report from metric/dimension names; normalizes property ID, executes runReport, reshapes parallel arrays into rows and returns rowCount.

tools.name: gtm_create
tools.description:
Create a GTM entity in a workspace (or a new workspace/environment in a container).

Defaults to dry-run: nothing is sent until called with dry_run=False.
Changes land in the workspace only — nothing goes live without gtm_publish.

entity_type.description: Entity to create: tags, triggers, variables, workspaces, ...

parent.description: Parent path: a container path for workspaces/environments, a workspace path for tags/triggers/variables/etc.
parent.title: Parent

body.description: Entity JSON per the GTM API, e.g. a tag: {'name': ..., 'type': 'gaawe', 'parameter': [...], 'firingTriggerId': [...]}. Read a similar existing entity with gtm_get to see the expected shape.
body.title: Body

dry_run.description: True (default) echoes the request without sending it.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

tools.behavior: Validates writable entity type and parent segment count. Dry-run echoes request; otherwise forwards arbitrary JSON to resource create.
notes: Enum includes read-only entities; handler restricts to workspaces, environments, tags, triggers, variables, folders, templates, clients, transformations, zones. Parent path validation checks segment count only.
Requires write/destructive tier; dry_run defaults true. Arbitrary dict bodies expose additionalProperties=true, not an API-specific body model.

tools.name: gtm_delete
tools.description:
Delete a GTM entity (tag, trigger, variable, workspace, version, ...). Two-phase.

Without confirm_token nothing is deleted; you get a summary + token to
confirm with. Deleting a workspace discards its unpublished changes.

path.description: Full path of the entity to delete, from gtm_list/gtm_get.
path.title: Path

confirm_token.description: Omit on the first call — it returns a token and a summary instead of deleting. Pass the token back (same path) to execute.
confirm_token.title: Confirm Token

tools.behavior: Validates deletable collection; first call issues a confirmation token, second matching call deletes the entity.
notes: Only workspaces, environments, tags, triggers, variables, folders, templates, clients, transformations, zones, versions collections may be deleted; accounts and containers excluded.
Requires destructive tier. Confirmation tokens are in-memory, single-use, expire after 600 seconds and bind to exact operation arguments; consumed before API execution.

tools.name: gtm_get
tools.description:
Fetch one GTM entity's complete JSON by its path (tag, trigger, variable, version, ...).

Note: fetching a version returns the entire published container (large).

path.description: Full GTM entity path from a gtm_list result, e.g. 'accounts/123/containers/456/workspaces/7/tags/8' or 'accounts/123/containers/456/versions/42'.
path.title: Path

tools.behavior: Validates alternating path segments, dispatches final collection to its discovery resource and gets full JSON.
notes: Handler checks even segment count and known final collection; schema only enforces nonempty string. Built-in-variable paths are dispatched to get without a special endpoint check.

tools.name: gtm_list

entity_type.description: Which GTM entity to list. Walk the hierarchy: accounts -> containers -> workspaces -> tags/triggers/variables/...

parent.description: Parent path from a previous result, e.g. '' for accounts, 'accounts/123' for containers, 'accounts/123/containers/456' for workspaces/versions/environments, 'accounts/123/containers/456/workspaces/7' for tags/triggers/variables.
parent.title: Parent

page_token.description: Pagination token from a previous response.
page_token.title: Page Token

full.description: Return complete entity JSON instead of trimmed summaries. Prefer gtm_get for a single entity.
full.title: Full

tools.behavior: Dispatches an entity type to a GTM resource list, validates parent segment count, returns full JSON or trimmed summaries and pagination token.
notes: Handler enforces parent segment count by entity, but does not validate collection names in parent path.

tools.name: gtm_permissions
tools.description:
Grant, update, or revoke a user's access to a GTM account. Two-phase.

Access changes are security-sensitive: always show the summary to the
user before confirming.

account_id.description: For 'grant': the GTM account ID, e.g. '123456'.
account_id.title: Account Id

path.description: For 'update'/'revoke': the permission path from gtm_list(user_permissions), e.g. 'accounts/123/user_permissions/456'.
path.title: Path

confirm_token.description: Omit first to get a summary + token; pass back to execute.
confirm_token.title: Confirm Token

tools.behavior: Validates action and conditional arguments; issues confirmation token, then creates, updates or deletes an account user permission.
notes: action is unconstrained string in schema; handler allows grant/update/revoke only. grant requires nonempty account_id/body; update requires path/body; revoke requires path.
Requires destructive tier. Confirmation tokens are in-memory, single-use, expire after 600 seconds and bind to exact operation arguments; consumed before API execution.

tools.name: gtm_publish
tools.description:
Compile a GTM workspace into a version and publish it LIVE. Two-phase.

Publishing deploys the container to every page that loads it — treat it
like a production release. The source workspace is consumed by versioning.

confirm_token.description: Omit on the first call — it returns a token and a summary instead of publishing. Pass the token back (same arguments) to execute.
confirm_token.title: Confirm Token

tools.behavior: First call issues confirmation. Redeeming compiles workspace into a version, checks compilerError and version path, then publishes the version live.
notes: Workspace path must have six nonempty segments and penultimate collection workspaces. Compilation consumes the source workspace before publish; compiler failure or missing version path aborts publishing.
Requires destructive tier. Confirmation tokens are in-memory, single-use, expire after 600 seconds and bind to exact operation arguments; consumed before API execution.

tools.name: gtm_update
tools.description:
Update (replace) a GTM entity by path. Defaults to dry-run.

GTM updates are full replacements — always start from gtm_get output.

path.description: Full path of the entity to update, from gtm_list/gtm_get.
path.title: Path

body.description: COMPLETE entity JSON (the GTM API replaces the entity, not merges). Fetch with gtm_get, modify, and send the whole object back.
body.title: Body

fingerprint.description: Optional optimistic-lock fingerprint from gtm_get; the update fails if someone changed the entity since.
fingerprint.title: Fingerprint

dry_run.description: True (default) echoes the request without sending it.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

tools.behavior: Validates path and writable collection. Dry-run echoes request; otherwise sends full replacement JSON to update with optional fingerprint.
notes: Only workspaces, environments, tags, triggers, variables, folders, templates, clients, transformations, zones collections may be updated. Body is intentionally unconstrained JSON and replaces the entity.
Requires write/destructive tier; dry_run defaults true. Arbitrary dict bodies expose additionalProperties=true, not an API-specific body model.
Source review only; no upstream execution, tools/list or live requests. HEAD matches supplied revision.

Inventory is full union of 16 tools: READ 8, WRITE 4, DESTRUCTIVE 4. Default advertises READ only (8); --allow-write or GTM_GA4_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE enables READ+WRITE (12); --allow-destructive or GTM_GA4_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE enables all (16). --deny TOOL and comma-separated GTM_GA4_MCP_DENY remove named tools at registration.

OAuth scopes are cumulative by tier and configured before registration; denylist does not reduce scopes. ADC clients are created lazily and cached per thread. No OAuth, GCP setup, auth, diagnostic, or support function is registered as a tool.
pyproject.toml uses mcp>=2,<3 and imports mcp.server.mcpserver.MCPServer (current v2 API); do not infer a v1 FastMCP import defect. Dependencies are not authenticated/runtime tested.

review.method: Independently compared all 16 function signatures/defaults/docstrings across seven registry modules; read Annotated Field bounds/descriptions and entity enums, merged ToolSpec registry, permission filtering, dry-run Admin writes and two-phase deletes/publishing. Default eight tools versus complete sixteen-tool union is documented.
